One assassination away from catastrophe: in June 1914, Europe was split into two armed camps. Here's how the tangled alliance system worked, and where it bent.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The Triple Alliance (red): Germany and Austria-Hungary had a Dual Alliance from 7 October 1879. Italy joined them on 20 May 1882.

2/ The Triple Entente (blue): France and Russia allied in 1894, France and Britain agreed the Entente Cordiale in 1904, and Britain and Russia signed their entente in 1907. Serbia (light blue) leaned on Russia.
3/ The spark: on 28 June 1914 Gavrilo Princip shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo.
4/ On 5-6 July Germany gave Austria-Hungary its 'blank cheque' of support. On 23 July Vienna sent Serbia an ultimatum with a 48-hour deadline, written so it would be rejected.

5/ On 25 July Russia secretly began a partial mobilisation, and Emperor Franz Joseph signed a mobilisation order against Serbia. Within days, the chain reaction of alliances spread across most of Europe.

6/ Britain entered the war on 4 August after Germany invaded Belgium. But look at Italy, red on this map: it declared neutrality, calling Austria-Hungary the aggressor, and joined the Entente side in 1915 via the Treaty of London.
Which of these surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
